newsitem.title: UK: Granada adds to Yorkshire-Tyne Tees stake.
newsitem.headline: Granada adds to Yorkshire-Tyne Tees stake.

text.p: British media and leisure company Granada raised its stake in Yorkshire-Tyne Tees Television on Wednesday after exercising more than 2.5 million Yorkshire warrants.
The move could take Granada's effective holding in YTTV to as high as 27 percent from its current level of some 24 percent.
Granada chief executive Charles Allen said that his company still had an open mind about a full bid for neighbour Yorkshire.
"We are still weighing up our options in relation to Yorkshire. Exercising warrants is consistent with whatever course of action we decide to take," he said.
Granada spent over 50 million stg in February on increasing its stake in Yorkshire by 10 percent to around 24 percent.
It had been expected to make a full bid for its neighbour following government approval earlier this year for an easing of media ownership laws.

The government has ended the two-licence limit on control of commercial television (ITV) franchises. It replaced it with an ownership ceiling of 15 percent of television audience, a move expected to trigger a wave of consolidation in the ITV sector.
Granada operates the ITV licences for north-west England and London Weekend Television (LWT).

Granada said in a statement that it had exercised 1,969,520 warrants in Yorkshire. It said the 1,969,520 Yorkshire shares arising from the exercise have been sold at Tuesday night's closing price of 1150 per share to Allquiet Investments, a deadlocked company owned jointly by Granada and Lazard Brothers.
Deadlocked companies have been used by media companies to hold excess stakes pending the new ownership rules which officially take effect on November 1.
Granada added that Allquiet had exercised 595,000 warrants in Yorkshire. Warrants could only be exercised within 10 working days of the publication of Yorkshire's results on September 3.
Yorkshire shares added 7.5p to 1157.5p on Wednesday while Granada lost 1p to 877.5p.
